config: catch-all submap rasklad_lock + device { name = hl-virtual-keyboard-unknown; keybinds = false }
findings: Under the catch-all submap the supervisor helper (keybinds=false) still delivers (20 events) while the stray virtual keyboard is blocked (0).

The runtime form works: hyprctl keyword device[hl-virtual-keyboard-unknown-1]:keybinds false unblocked the stray keyboard at once (0 -> 20), so per-device exemption can be set at arm time, no config reload.

Consequence: the exemption is keyed by device name only. Names are assigned by order (unknown, unknown-1); the supervisor must check that exactly one exempt device exists and that it is its own before arming, and must never exempt more.
Not measured: the physical wl_keyboard (no host input by policy); it is a normal keyboard subject to the same catch-all. F12 inside the submap is bound for it.
